correctness.rationale: Exact unitary Fourier diagonalization gives every finite-window probability by a finite spectral-pair sum. Only diagonal and opposite-index energies collide at zero flux. Their arguments converge to a universal scaled sine, with a bounded-error estimate from the elementary integral-kernel derivative. Fourier-frequency coefficient uniqueness (odd dimensions) and paired coefficients (even dimensions) reduce uniformity to simultaneous zeros of the sinc kernel. The ratio of two required frequency splittings is a rational algebraic integer equal to \(2\cos(2\pi/n)\), impossible in its strict nonintegral ranges except the three explicitly resolved sizes. All boundaries and the simple-spectrum generic-flux regime are handled. Numeric quadrature is corroborative, not a substitute for these proofs.
